# frontend specification

> Status: design settled (**v2 = Console v2 + capture store**). Fully reorganized from v1 (feature tabs) into **role tabs**, and then every screen was moved off runs/episodes onto **captures**. The Japanese version is canonical (treat it as the source of truth). The English version `docs/specs/en/frontend.md` is an auto-generated mirror (do not edit it directly). **No authentication is required.**

A backend-driven, lightweight Web UI (Vite + React + TypeScript). Tabs are organized not by technical function (v1: Live / Graph / Probe / Recordings / Validation / Datasets / Config) but by **"whose job is it"** — 6 tabs: **Collect / Review / Datasets / Validation / Monitor / Settings**.

## Roles

| Tab | Whose job | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Collect | Operator | Run recordings, judge immediately, improve |
| Review | ML engineer | Judge recording quality and labels, feed them into datasets |
| Datasets | ML engineer | Compose logical datasets, catalog them, (future) build them |
| Validation | Robot engineer | Run pipelines, standardize validation |
| Monitor | Robot engineer | Diagnose communication, signals, the system and **store health** |
| Settings | Robot engineer | Robot configuration, plans, and their scope of effect |

Core concept: **recording quality and task result are separate axes** (a failed task ≠ bad data; failure data is kept, labeled, and used for training). Recording proceeds in a **Batch > Episode** hierarchy persisted by the orchestrator ([api_orchestrator.md](api_orchestrator.md) "Batch"; the Session level is **TBD**: Phase 2.5).

**What v2 (capture store) changes across every screen**:

- **Every screen reads the `captures` API.** Not one call to `/api/v1/runs` or `/api/v1/episodes` remains. v1's feature tabs (`RunsTab` / `DatasetTab` / `inspect`) and the in-browser bridge `episodeBridge` have been **deleted**.
- **testids are keyed by `capture_id`** (by `membership_id` for dataset members). Never by row number or by position within a batch — two batches holding the same number would collide.
- **The Availability chip** (below) states, in one vocabulary across every screen, whether a recording's bytes are on this machine right now.
- **Deletion is two separate dialogs, Discard and Delete** (below).
- Monitor gained a **Store health panel** (rebuild / corrupt / SUSPECT / Repair).

## Implementation

- Base: **Vite + React + TypeScript**.
- State: **Zustand** (UI state) + **TanStack Query** (server state; SSE events are folded into the cache). Routing is URL-query based (`?tab=<id>`).
- Charts: unified on **uPlot** (axis ticks, crosshair, series overlay, zoom). UI: **Tailwind CSS** (components are hand-rolled).
- Live video: **WebRTC** (connects to `webrtc_streamer`'s `/stream/offer`).
- Tests: **Vitest + Testing Library**.

## Inputs

- WebRTC video (`webrtc_streamer`; by default same-origin via `/webrtc`, reverse-proxied by the frontend's nginx; override with `WEBRTC_PUBLIC_URL`)
- Numeric-field sample streams (`topic_probe`; same-origin via `/probe`; used by Monitor's Signals view)
- REST / SSE (`api_orchestrator` `/api/v1`)

## Tabs and navigation

- **The 6 tabs are fixed in the frontend** (`V2_TABS`). v1's "driven by the backend `tabs` registry" mechanism is **retired** — the `tabs` field of `GET /api/v1/config` remains for compatibility, but v2 does not use it for display or ordering.
- **All legacy tab ids redirect** to preserve deep links: `live`→`collect`, `graph`/`probe`→`monitor`, `runs`→`review`, `dataset`→`datasets`, `config`→`settings`.
- Every tab is URL-addressable (`?tab=<id>`). **`?tab=<id>&solo=1` renders only that tab, with no tab bar** (the ↗ button on each tab opens it in a separate window — the multi-window way to line up several charts).
- **Header (shared by all tabs)**: the 6 tabs, a **ROS_DOMAIN_ID badge**, a **connection chip** (the SSE connection state), and an **OP chip** — click it to set the operator name (persisted in localStorage; sent as `operator` on every subsequent `/record/start`).

## Parts shared by every screen (v2)

### The Availability chip

Derived from `capture.replica.state` and `capture.digest_state` by a **single decision function**, and drawn as the same chip by Review / Datasets / Validation. "Is it usable" (`usable`) is a value derived from this chip, and it is the shared precondition for running jobs, previewing, and archiving.

| replica.state | Display | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `null` (no row) | not here yet | No copy on this machine yet. **Normal in the split deployment** (you pull from the robot after review). Not an error |
| `present_verified` | verified | Here, and the digest has been confirmed to match |
| `present_unverified` + `digest_state=pending` | verifying | Here, but verification is still running |
| `present_unverified` | here | Here |
| `trashed` | in trash | In `.trash` (awaiting the reaper) |
| `absent_managed` | removed | kairos deleted it deliberately |
| `missing_unmanaged` | missing | **It disappeared outside of kairos.** A warning |
| `corrupt` | corrupt | The sidecar cannot be read. A warning |
| an unknown value | unknown | A state this console does not know. **Surfaced as a warning** (the server may be newer = treat the whereabouts of the bytes as unconfirmed) |

The point is to **never blur `verifying` into `verified`**. Show something as "verified" before it has been verified, and the display stops meaning anything at all.

### The two deletion dialogs (Discard / Delete)

**They are deliberately not one shared component.** Fold two things whose wording, required fields and weight of confirmation differ into a single part, and a change to one leaks into the other.

| | Discard (not uploaded) | Delete |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Discarding data that was never uploaded | Ordinary deletion |
| reason | **Mandatory** (an empty field disables the confirm button) | Optional |
| Wording | States plainly that it cannot be undone and there is no restore | "The files go away, but the catalog keeps the record, so we can still answer where they went" |
| Count · size | Always shows the number of items and the byte total (`(size unknown)` if not known) | Same |

- The reason the reason is mandatory is stated right there: "it goes into the lifecycle ledger; once the files are gone, that one line is the only record of why they were deleted".
- **In the split deployment both dialogs carry the caveat that a copy stays on the robot** (split is detected from `available` in `GET /api/v1/transfer/status`). The discard side says it honestly: "this deployment records on a separate robot. What is discarded is **the copy on this recording PC**; a copy may remain on the robot, and kairos does not delete it."
- Bulk runs are sequential, show progress (`{done}/{n}`), and **report failures honestly, per capture**. Cancel is blocked while a bulk run is in flight.
- `409 capture_busy` comes back naming the lease holder and its expiry ("wait for that job to finish, then retry").

## Screens

### Collect — run recordings and judge immediately

- **Context bar**: Robot (real selection; the same robot catalog as Settings) / Project · Task · Condition (pickers fed by Plans, plus Custom free input) / **Batch number** / episode progress "n / target".
  - **The Plans catalog (Projects → Tasks → Conditions) is server-synced** (2026-07-14): reconciled once per load against `GET/PUT /api/v1/plans` — a never-set server is **seeded** from this browser's catalog, unsynced local edits (a dirty flag that survives reloads) are pushed, otherwise the server copy is adopted. Offline, the browser-local catalog stands and a dirty edit is re-pushed on the next edit/load. Keeping condition a picker keeps the label vocabulary from fragmenting across terminals (the batch-label decision).
  - The batch number is the **server-issued `batch_seq`** (per robot × local date, restarting from 1 each morning). Before a batch exists, show a **prediction** — "next #N · assigned on first recording" (today's max seq + 1) — which settles to the server value on the first recording. There is no "planned batch count" denominator (it has no real referent).
- **Batch / Episode progress is server-persisted**: the batch is created lazily on the first recording (`POST /api/v1/batches`). An empty batch has no row and consumes no number. Reloads / tab switches restore via `GET /api/v1/batches?status=active`.
- **Batch menu** semantics (End early / Reset **never delete recordings**):
  - Pause / Resume (currently local only; server-side is **TBD**: Phase 2.5) / End batch early (`status=ended_early` + reason) / Reset (a **complete no-op** for an empty batch; with recordings it closes the current batch and the next recording starts a new number) / Change condition (PATCH) / **Change target (2026-07-14)**: set the batch's planned `target_episodes` (1–500, PATCH; inherited by the next batch; lowering it below the recorded count is flagged up front as completing the batch immediately). **The strip's chip count, "n / target" and the completion check all follow the target** (the UI's fixed 30 is gone — a value the API always had and the UI ignored) / Report issue.
- **Recording controls**: Start / Stop. **Pre-arm (two-phase start, 2026-07-14)**: on a robot with `recording.pre_arm` (default on), while the tab is visible and the phase is ready/result the screen keeps the recorder armed via `POST /record/prepare` (a keep-alive re-prepare just before `disarm_at`; best-effort — failures are never surfaced, Start simply falls back to the conventional full synchronous path). While armed, a "pre-armed · instant start" chip sits next to the Start button and the SYSTEM STATUS Recorder row shows `ARMED` (both **read the server-reported state** — never lit merely because a prepare was sent). The Required data row also gets real measurements before recording, from the armed session's subscription snapshot. Arming gate (waits for subscriptions to be established; an "N matched · N missing" note), failed-start banner (**plain wording leads, the raw code follows** — `already_recording` and the rest are mapped into operator language), **recorder cache/drop detection banner** (`dropped_messages` + a cache-setting hint, gated to that capture). **Keyboard**: `R`=Start / `S`·`Space`=Stop / `Esc`=Cancel arming / `?`=shortcut list (disabled while an input field is focused; button labels carry a hint such as `· R`). On each phase transition, focus moves to the next primary action (never falls to the body).
- **Recording state is server-truth** (5s polling of `GET /record/status`; HCD fix 2026-07-14): if a recording this browser did not start, or has lost sight of, is running, a **RECORDING IN PROGRESS card** (run_id / elapsed / size / operator / topics, a `Stop & save` behind a confirm modal, `Open in Monitor →`) appears instead of READY. The Recorder row of SYSTEM STATUS comes from the same query = the "READY yet 409" contradiction cannot arise structurally. A take recovered by stopping shows up under "Unsaved-take recovery" below. Record-topic resolution matches v1 (selected / configured / all; the selection is shared with Monitor's Rec column, and the "REC N topics" chip jumps to Monitor; Start is disabled on an empty selection).
- **Saving an episode**: Stop → a real-event gate (resolve the stop API → **confirm the recorder stopped** → read integrity; the fixed timer is retired, and a failed stop stays in SAVING with `Retry stop`) → the result panel. **A `200` from stop is not enough to move forward on (2026-07-27)**: `POST /record/stop` is idempotent and, when it cannot find anything active, answers `200` with the most recent run — so **a recording that is still going looks like a success**. After it resolves, `GET /record/status` is therefore checked; still `recording`/`stopping` routes it into the existing `STOP_FAILED` path and it stays in SAVING (`Retry stop`). Without that, the screen advances to labelling a take that is still being written, and the only thing left to end it is the `MAX_RECORD_SECONDS` auto-stop. **Success is the default selection**, so a clean success is a single `Save — success` action (Enter works). Failure branches from ✕ with a mandatory reason. **The automatic quality prefers the server's settled `quick_check.verdict`**, falling back to the real integrity only while it is still unsettled (clean → `Good · auto`; drop/failed → `Needs review · auto` plus the real drop count — nothing is made up). It can be overridden freely from `change` with the three choices (good / needs_review / not_usable). **Saving is `PATCH /api/v1/captures/{id}/review`** (a CAS that requires `base_revision`). The payload sends `quality` + `quality_source='operator'` only on an override; with no override it omits `quality`/`quality_source` and lets the server derive them (the capture's settled `quick_check.verdict` is the single source of the automatic quality; even when the save lands before settlement the server corrects it afterwards — [api_orchestrator.md](api_orchestrator.md) "Late re-derivation after settlement"). The operator's steps and keystrokes are unchanged (the omission is a payload-side change only). **Only once the server has settled, a receipt** `Saved — Episode n of Batch m · {operator}` (a transient ring on the strip chip). Discard is a **real delete** that goes through the Discard dialog (**reason mandatory**; "The two deletion dialogs" above) — `POST /api/v1/captures/{id}/delete {kind:"discard"}`.
- **Unsaved-take recovery**: even if you leave between Stop and Save, on reload an amber banner "Unsaved take from {time} — {N} MB, {duration}" (`Label it` / `Discard` / `Later`) lets you recover it (it detects the most recent capture that is in a terminal state and has `review_revision == 0`).
- The "n / target" count is the **monotone counter `episodes_recorded`** (what was recorded is the truth; a deletion in Review never decreases it; if it diverges from the quality breakdown, a footnote says so).
- **COVERAGE side card**: per condition of the current task, it shows the **recorded count** (Σ `episodes_recorded` over this task's batches — the first review save advances it and nothing afterwards ever lowers it, so it survives a later exclude / delete). Rows = the plan's conditions ∪ the conditions actually used in batches; the currently-selected condition is highlighted. It exists so that **"what to record next" is decided from data**, and the counting method is spelled out in a footnote (no fabricated values).
  - **The "exported" column was dropped in v2.** Under §6 a dataset became a named set of captures and has no condition of its own, so the old count **has no source left to derive it from**. Better to show no number at all than a number nobody can derive.
- **The episode strip places each chip on its true episode number (`index_in_batch`)**: drawing by array position lets a deletion in Review pack the later chips leftward, producing the off-by-one where the newest episode reads as "not recorded". A recorded number with nothing surviving behind it is distinguished honestly by a dashed chip plus "recorded earlier; no longer listed (deleted in Review)". When the server re-allocated the `index_in_batch` of a save (a cross-terminal collision), the response value is adopted for the local chip too. **The server restore merges only within the same batch** (so a just-saved chip does not flip back to not recorded). A restore onto a different batch never carries the local count over.
- **Cameras**: WebRTC previews. Panes can be added/removed (max 4). The main pane has resolution presets; sub panes are force-capped to low resolution (240/360p). **Latency / fps live in an overlay chip at the top-right inside the preview video** (per-tile measured values, threshold colors; never placed outside the video). Pre-connect placeholders state the reason for their state (an empty tile must not read as a failure).
- **Active warnings card (extended 2026-07-15, revised 2026-07-27)**: the union of two real-data signals — ① the arming snapshot's uncaptured targets (current values while `armed`, frozen at start-time while recording) + ② **firing monitor alerts** (the SSE `alert` buffer; hz/gap threshold breaches = **mid-recording degradation**, surfaced on the screen the operator is looking at). ① **never merges the causes**: only `missing_topics` (no publisher) is asserted as "N target topics not publishing", while `unsubscribed_topics` (published, recorder not subscribed yet) gets its own "not subscribed yet" wording — displaying a topic that Monitor shows at 30 Hz as "not publishing" is a lie, and it sends the operator off to fix the wrong thing (with both present it asserts neither: "not being captured" + the breakdown). Alerts are **restricted to the recorded topics** (the arming matched∪missing∪unsubscribed set when present, else the config `default_topics` patterns, else everything — broader beats silently hidden). Rows carry the measured value (`joint_states Hz < 45 · now 38.2`), cap at 2 + "+N more in Monitor", with an "Open in Monitor →" path. Shown while idle too (so you notice "the robot is off today" before you start recording). The System status card gains a **Topic rates row** (`N / M at expected` — of the topics the monitor judged, how many are status=ok; `unknown` stays out of the denominator, and "—" when the monitor is down). No composite score is built (it would hide the causes).
- **Quick check** (the post-stop quality summary): the result panel shows the `quick_check.verdict` the server settled at stop time (good / needs_review + human-readable `reasons`), polled gently from the capture detail `GET /api/v1/captures/{id}` (~3 tries / 5s, stopping once settled). While unsettled it shows only a subtle "Quick check running…" note (nothing is made up), and **saving never waits on settlement**. The evaluation is designed as a two-layer "settlement of the monitoring statistics accumulated during recording" — Layer 0 = the statistics the monitor / recorder hold during recording (counts, drops, gaps, expected_hz ratio; final at stop), Layer 1 = read only the MCAP summary section (O(index)). It must hold **in ≤5 s with zero transfer, even in the split deployment** (details in [api_orchestrator.md](api_orchestrator.md) "Stop-time quick check").
- **Advice** is a single fixed mock (hold still ~1s). **Generation logic is TBD (Phase 3)**. Only the approach is settled: live advice takes the orchestrator's aggregated SSE metrics as input; deep advice takes the transferred MCAP (dora never touches DDS).
- Fits **without scrolling** from 1920×1080 down to 1366×768 (compact density toggle).

### Review — judge quality and labels, feed datasets

- List + detail of completed recordings. Each row is one capture (`GET /api/v1/captures`) and shows **Batch "MM/DD · #N" / Task result / Quality / lane / the Availability chip**. Filterable by operator and so on. **The list follows the cursor all the way to the end** (it does not silently cut off at 200), and the header carries real-data tally chips (`n ready · n needs check · n excluded` / `n success · n failure`). The displayed number is the **persistent `index_in_batch`** (a deletion never renumbers it). The decision buttons are a **fixed bar outside the scroll**.
- **Exception-review model**: a capture whose quality is good (or operator-confirmed) is **READY** with no extra click. Only **NEEDS CHECK** (quality not good and still unjudged) forms the work queue, resolved with "Mark OK — include" or Exclude. The default order is NEEDS CHECK → READY → EXCLUDED.
- **Review saves are a genuine CAS** (`PATCH /api/v1/captures/{id}/review`; [api_orchestrator.md](api_orchestrator.md) "Saving a review"). **Nothing is optimistically committed** — the optimistic edit is displayed, but it is rolled back if the save fails.
  - **`409` (conflict)**: a banner stating "someone else saved first. Reload and re-apply your edit — the two edits are not merged", and it **names the value currently stored on the server** (`It is now {review_status} · {quality}`). To do that it re-fetches `GET /api/v1/captures/{id}` best-effort.
  - **`500` (the sidecar write failed)**: a red banner that **must be dismissed explicitly**: "**Not saved.** …nothing was saved — `record.json` could not be written. Fix the free space or the permissions, then save again". It must never disappear on its own like a toast (if it does, you walk away believing a save happened when it did not).
- **Datasets is the entry point for feeding a dataset** (one function, one place). Review carries the judgement, and once READY is reached it offers the path to Datasets. v1's **move** via "Export ready (n)…" is gone — a dataset became a logical set, and the recorded bytes do not move ([capture_store](capture_store.md) §6).
- **Deletion is two-step**: Exclude = "Excluded — kept on disk" (non-destructive, label only) → only the excluded items get the Delete / Discard path ("The two deletion dialogs" above; bulk runs sequentially and reports failures honestly). From EXCLUDED and from confirmed exceptions, "↩ Return to review" puts the item back to pending (reversible).
- **Detail inspection**: manifest / validation / loss_report table / on-demand mp4 "Video check" player / each JSON block. `fast_validation` can also be run from the detail.
- **Data integrity section (the former Signals section, redesigned 2026-07-15)**: runs `signal_report` behind an explicit button and shows, in order, **① the synced video (video_check's full-length mp4) → ② the aggregated integrity timeline directly beneath it → ③ a ranked loss-event table → ④ a per-topic summary (message count · continuity · loss-event count)**. The timeline is **one lane** (the worst condition across all topics overlaid: green = nothing wrong / amber = minor / red = major, or silence on a dense topic / gray = no topic active); hovering names the degraded topics, clicking seeks the video (only when the full-length video is loaded — with a head-only preview it would be a lie, so it is disabled). **Empty bin = red is restricted to dense topics (median non-zero density ≥ 3)** — measured on real data, the bin width (~10 ms) fell below the message period (20–30 ms) and painted healthy data solid red. Loss on sparse topics is carried by the backend's loss_events (1.5× the median interval). The event table ranks **majors first, then by duration descending**, shows the first 8, and folds the rest behind an explicit "Show all n events" (the count is always visible = nothing is hidden silently). **The former raw waveform chart (the per-field uPlot plot) and the field-picker UI were removed** (a raw joint-angle waveform does not answer "is this episode usable"; live waveforms are Monitor > Signals = topic_probe). The Settings signals-defaults editor and `GET/PUT /api/v1/config/signals` were removed along with it.
- **Batch filter + batch-level bulk decisions**: clicking a row's batch chip narrows the list to that batch (click again / ✕ / Clear to leave). While filtered, the header offers "Exclude batch (n)…" (with a confirm modal, and the same reversible semantics as the single-row Exclude: Not usable + excluded, **the recordings stay on disk**, sequential saves, per-row failures reported honestly) and "↺ Return batch (n)" (bulk-restores the excluded ones to pending). One action to keep a batch that FAILed batch-level validation (Validation) out of the mix. Section-grouping of the list (full grouping) is **deliberately not adopted** — it would break the exception-review work order (NEEDS CHECK first).
- **Failure reasons are visible**: the `failure_reason` picked at save time is shown as the tooltip of the list's FAILURE chip and, in red, under the detail panel's Task result field.
- **Transfer in the split deployment**: split is detected from `available` in `GET /api/v1/transfer/status`, and when it applies, alongside the Availability chip's `not here yet` a "transfer to the recording PC" action appears (`POST /api/v1/transfer/pull {capture_id}`). **Completion is not announced by the transfer API** — what the frontend watches is the capture's **replica state**, which turns `present_unverified` the moment the reconciler adopts the arrived directory. v1's `bag_local` boolean was retired (it could only say "here / not here", and **could not tell a copy that never arrived from a copy that was deliberately removed**). Transfer is **manual pull only** (no automatic scheduler is being built), and **transfer and validation are separate buttons** (never auto-chained). Auto-pull on the first review save is opt-in via `transfer.auto_pull_on_save`.

### Datasets — composing logical datasets, and the catalog

**In v2 a dataset became a logical set** ([capture_store](capture_store.md) §6). The recorded bytes never move out of `objects/<capture_id>`; a dataset is nothing but a DB row plus ledger events. This tab is therefore not "the catalog of what has been exported" but "**the place where sets are composed**".

- **Composition**: add to a dataset from the candidate rail (captures that reached READY in Review) with `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/members`, and remove with `DELETE …/members/{membership_id}`. **Not one byte moves**, so taking something out and putting it back, or putting one capture into several datasets, is free. `display_index` never reuses a gap.
- **Label editing**: the header's "Edit" (rendered only while active) → a three-field modal for name / operator / task (`PATCH /datasets/{id}`). The dialog states explicitly that the members and their numbers do not change. A dataset recorded by several people may leave operator empty (every recording keeps its own operator).
- **Combine**: the left column's "⧉ Combine" → a name for the new dataset plus the sources (a checklist of active datasets, pick order = numbering order) → run. **The sources are never written to** (a dataset is a list, and reading a list does not change it). The implementation is nothing but the ordinary create + add-member in bulk, under the standing bulk rule (sequential, `{done}/{n}` progress, per-capture failures listed honestly, Cancel blocked while running). A capture present in two sources joins once, at its first appearance. Archiving the new combined dataset later runs into the shared-member `409`, so the sources must be cleared up first (deleted, or the members removed) — deleting a dataset touches no recording.
- **URL state is held as `dataset_id` / `membership_id`** (`url.ts` owns only the `ds*` keys and never touches `tab` / `solo`). **Names are editable and `display_index` is for display**, so these two are the only stable ids. A URL that specifies `dsmem` with no `dsid` is dropped.
- **Label filters + manifest**: task-result chips (All / Success / Failure) + an operator select + a search box narrow the list. "Manifest (n)" downloads the filtered result as a JSON manifest (`data_dir`-relative paths + every label) — **materializing the training-set definition as one version-controllable file**. When everything is hidden it says so explicitly: "n hidden by the filter".
- Every member row and candidate row carries the **Availability chip** (above). **A capture that is not usable (missing / trashed / not here yet) is never a target for a job, a preview, or an archive.**
- Detail = DatasetDetail (metadata / member list / topics / loss report / mp4 Video check / sidecar JSON). Jobs run against `capture_id` (`params.dataset_dir` is retired).
- **Per-capture archive**: the button appears only when the candidate meets all three conditions — "an archive root is configured", "it is a member of no dataset", and "its availability is usable". The dialog shows **both** the destination and `<destination>/<capture_id>`, and the confirm label is "Copy, verify, then remove".
  - **If verification fails, never pretend it succeeded**: `Copied to {dest}, but it did NOT verify — check it before trusting the copy`. On success: `Archived to {dest} — verified, then removed from this machine`.
- **Per-dataset archive (§6.1, the terminal transition)**: the header's "Archive dataset" appears **only when it can succeed** (a root is configured, the status is active, and there is at least one member). The dialog gives the same boundary presentation as the per-capture one (a root picker plus a subpath input, and a **double echo** of the destination being sent and the `<destination>/<operator>/<task>/<name>` that will actually be written — the last three components are the server's), plus a **mode radio**: "Copy out — keep them" (seal only; confirm label "Copy, verify, then seal") and "Move out — remove them" (deletes the sources; "Copy, verify, then remove"). When members are shared with another active dataset, **Copy is the default and the dialog says why (n shared)** — a Move the server would refuse with a 409 enumerating them. The archived banner also keeps the modes honestly apart (Copied to … stays on this machine / Archived to … removed from this machine). After the `202`, **the same dialog turns into a progress view**, polling `GET /datasets/{id}/archive` at 1-second intervals and drawing `{done} / {total}`, the capture being copied, and the halt reason. **A halt is not a failure to be dismissed**: the run stays `archiving`, and Resume (a re-POST with no destination) picks up from where it stopped. The completion toast is `Archived to {dir} — n recordings verified, then removed from this machine`.
  - **The status is a badge, part of the row's identity** (archiving = amber, archived = gray, on both the list row and the header). archived is read-only: a banner names the destination and when, and the members' Remove / Discard / Delete and the BuildRail's add controls are **not rendered** (the server refuses them all with `409`, so putting them up would be putting up buttons guaranteed to fail). The dataset's Delete is disabled with "Kept: this record is what remembers where the dataset went." — **the archived row is the queryable cache of the migration log** and is never deletable.
- **Delete** ("The two deletion dialogs" above). Deleting the dataset itself is `DELETE /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}`, and it **never touches the captures' bytes** (archiving / archived are `409`, as above).
- **Build** (conversion to LeRobot v3 and the like) and **Recipe-style dataset construction are unimplemented (TBD: Phase 2)** — the UI shows muted shells only, never dressed up as working controls.

### Validation — pipeline execution, standardized

Keeps v1's functionality as-is; only the layout is v2.

- **Pipeline-agnostic**: pick a pipeline (every enabled one from `GET /api/v1/pipelines`) → **pick the targets**: captures (v2 has lost the "before / after export" distinction, so there is neither grouping nor a `dataset_dir` branch; only captures whose availability is usable can be targeted) → **the parameter form** (auto-generated from `schemas.pipeline_forms[<id>]`; an `x-suggest`-annotated string becomes a picker over the target capture's real topics, with the first one auto-seeded — video_check's `topic` needs no hand-typed camera path) → run (`POST /api/v1/jobs {capture_id, pipeline, params}`). Results are drawn by a **generic renderer** that renders `summary.json` shape-independently (PASS/FAIL badge, message, a key-value tree of metrics, artifacts, raw JSON). **An artifact whose path is data-relative (normalised by the orchestrator) is rendered as fetchable via `GET /api/v1/files/{path}`**: images (png/jpg/svg/gif/webp) render **inline**, anything else becomes a download link, and an absolute path that cannot be normalised stays plain text (never fabricate a link that would 404). So **a plugin that writes a plot image into its report dir gets a graph in the UI with no UI changes**. **Adding a plugin requires no edits to this tab** ([dora_plugins.md §2.5](dora_plugins.md)).
- Only the bundled `fast_validation` has a dedicated checklist against the template's required-topic list. Results can be downloaded as CSV.
- **Bulk execution**: "All completed captures" submits the selected pipeline to every capture in a terminal state (one `POST /api/v1/jobs` per capture). A per-capture progress list (live state; PASS/FAIL on completion).
- **Per-batch bulk validation** (the blast-radius decision = bulk validation only, no alert persistence): the target selector gains a "Batches" group. Picking a batch submits the selected pipeline to **every capture in that batch** (candidates = the captures belonging to that batch whose availability is usable; the unusable ones are shown as out of scope, with the reason). The entry point for verifying, in one click, defects that cluster per batch such as calibration drift.
- **One-click validation presets**: preset buttons from `GET /api/v1/validation/presets` (`pipeline` + fixed `params`). Bulk-run against **not-yet-validated captures** (`pending_capture_ids`). Shows "N pending"; at zero it is disabled as "up to date". Defined in the per-robot config `config/<robot>/validation_presets.yaml` ([config.md](config.md)).
- Lifecycle chips (Experimental → Standard promotion) are **visual only (TBD: substance later)**.

### Monitor — communication, signal and system diagnostics

The merge target for v1's Graph / Probe / Live health panels. The sub-nav is **Overview / Topics / Signals / System / Store / Events / Logs**. Every sub-view is built on real data (unobtainable values show "—"; an empty chart or empty list states why). The default view is Overview.

- **Context strip**: REC · run_id · elapsed while recording, STANDBY otherwise (a real display, from `record_status`).
- **Overview view** (the diagnostic landing, default): the record context, a topic-health tally (`ok`/`warning`/`danger`/`inactive` counts + the topics needing attention by name → click to chart them in Topics), a summary of firing incidents (the real alert buffer), a compact `GET /api/v1/system` snapshot, and jumps to Topics/Signals.
- **Topics view**:
  - **Add / remove chart panels (max 4)**. Per panel, pick a metric (**Frequency / Bandwidth / Max gap / Rate vs expected**) and the topic overlay (max 6). The time window (30s / 1m / 5m) and **Freeze charts / Live** (formerly Pause) are global — the freeze is charts-only (it says so: `Charts frozen · table still live.`; the table deliberately stays live). Since the window accumulates from when it was opened, while the accumulation is shorter than the window it honestly shows `{window} window (n so far)`. Chart height **follows the measured slot** (the root fix for the bug where a fixed height was clipped by an overflow-hidden parent and the low value range became invisible). **The recording's REC / STOP markers** overlay every panel. Frequency carries the expected_hz reference line. **Latency / loss are not on the menu** — a non-intrusive monitor cannot measure them (per-run loss is provided by Review's post-hoc analysis).
  - **Topics table**: every discovered topic + live metrics (Hz / bandwidth / gap, status dot `inactive`/`danger`/`warning`/`ok`/`unknown`, a shortfall badge with a reason tooltip on threshold breach; shortfall is observed, not true loss). **The Rec checkbox column** = the topic selection for the next recording (not a mid-recording change). Configured topics are pre-checked. Switching robots reseeds from the config defaults. Independent of the chart series selection.
- **Signals view** (v1 Probe, ported): a generic plotter that overlays the **numeric fields** from `topic_probe` per (topic, field). Pick a topic → a numeric field (arrays expand to `[0..N]`), and **overlay several fields across different topics**. Sample-rate selection (1/5/10/30 Hz, default 10 Hz), window, Pause. **Decoding is carried by the isolated `topic_probe` container and never spills into recording or monitoring** ([topic_probe.md](topic_probe.md)).
- **System view** (full page): host measurements (CPU% / GPU% / disk usage · `GET /api/v1/system`; unobtainable values show "—") + ROS_DOMAIN_ID / service endpoints (`GET /api/v1/config`) + **component health**. Health is expressed only from signals the browser can honestly observe: orchestrator = the live SSE pipe being open, monitor = the `bridge` event. It states explicitly that per-container recorder / streamer readiness is judged by the orchestrator's **server-side `/readyz`** (for the Docker healthcheck) and is not exposed at the browser origin (`/readyz` is not proxied on the same origin, so it is not fetched). A compact **System card** is embedded in the Overview / Topics right rail.
- **Store view (new in v2)**: polls `GET /api/v1/store/health` every 30 seconds to surface **the states that never appear in the capture list** ([api_orchestrator.md](api_orchestrator.md) "Store health and SUSPECT").
  - **The SUSPECT block**: "Suspect — automatic clean-up is halted" + the reason + the time it latched. It **spells out both what is halted and what is not** (halted: the automatic missing transition, the reaper, digests / not halted: recording, saving reviews, browsing). It states that it does not re-fire on every pass, and that only a repair clears it.
  - **The Repair button** is enabled only under SUSPECT. `409 volume_unidentified` is displayed with its reason and disables the button. On success both the store-health and the captures caches are invalidated.
  - **The corrupt list**: path, reason and capture id, plus **which scan it came from** (`corrupt_source` of `reconcile` reads as "reconciler pass", otherwise "rebuild") and the time it was observed. An empty display **distinguishes** the two cases: "no scan has run to completion in this process yet — this is not an all-clear" and "the last {rebuild|reconciler pass} could read every sidecar it found".
  - **Whether deletion is available** (`delete_available` / `delete_unavailable_reason`): when `objects/` and `.trash/` are on different filesystems, it explains on the spot why the deletion APIs return `503`.
  - **The rebuild summary** (`rebuilt_at` + the breakdown) and the **warnings**, plus the most recent reconcile result.
  - If reading the health itself fails, it says "**the store's state could not be read, so nothing below is known — this is not an all-clear**". Blankness is never dressed up as "nothing wrong".
- **Events**: SSE `alert`s **collapsed to one row per incident (topic × metric)** — while firing, `firing · since {t}` updates the current value in place; on clearing it flips to `cleared · {t}` (muted); a re-fire shows `×n`. The **Events card** in the Overview / Topics right rail shows the collapsed rows; the **Events view** (full page) adds a topic substring + state (firing/cleared/all) filter and a note (history is session-local, since Monitor was opened). Topics with no config rule are picked up too, by the monitor's default DANGER incident (persisting ~10s) = **the table's DANGER and Events do not contradict each other** ([topic_monitor.md](topic_monitor.md)).
- **Logs view**: a session-local timeline of the SSE lifecycle events received (record_status / alert / job) with type chips + a text filter (a ring buffer capped at ~500). Honestly labelled "since this page opened / the full logs live in `docker compose logs`". Metrics are not recorded (high-frequency noise).

### Settings — robot configuration and plans

- **Robots**: the robot list (committed `config/<robot>/` and gitignored `config/local/<robot>/`) and selection (`POST /api/v1/config/select` hot-swaps recording / stream; recorder QoS / monitor expected_hz apply after a restart — the UI says so. **Activating while recording shows a "Stop and switch?" confirm modal**). **A non-active robot's config is viewable read-only** (`GET /api/v1/config/robots/{robot}`; a "Read-only — {robot} is not the active robot." banner + disabled JSON that can be read as a template). **Aspect** (recording / stream / validation / validators) option selection. The recording config is edited and persisted as JSON (`PUT /api/v1/config/recording`. **Inline validation**: invalid JSON disables Save with a plain error; saving while recording shows an "applies from the next recording" info banner). Creating a new robot is not possible — `+ Add robot` opens not a disappearing toast but a **persistent explainer that shows the next step** (create a `config/<robot>/` folder + use an existing robot as a template). The bottom of the rail retires the sourceless version display in favour of the **active robot's real values**.
- **Projects & tasks (Plans)**: edit the Project / Task / Condition definitions. A **shared store** with Collect's pickers reflects them immediately, and they are **persisted server-side** (`PUT /api/v1/plans`. 2026-07-14 — one label vocabulary shared across every terminal. Offline, localStorage stands and dirty edits are re-pushed later. **Modelling** Plans (ids/references/target counts) remains Phase 2.5).
- **Recording**: the active robot's recording config shown **form-first** (`GET /api/v1/config/recording`: compression / start gate [`start_paused`] / cache [`max_cache_size_mb`] and the default_topics table [expected Hz, QoS-override badge]). The raw JSON editor is demoted to "Advanced" (collapsed by default, `PUT /api/v1/config/recording`).
- **Data quality**: from the aspect content of `GET /api/v1/config/robots/{robot}` — the expected-Hz reference rates + the monitor's warn/danger thresholds (`monitor.warn_shortfall`/`danger_shortfall`) + the active validation template's required topics (a read-only card). Beneath it, the **alert-rules editor** (`GET/PUT /api/v1/config/alerts` → `config/<robot>/monitoring/alerts.yaml`. It applies on monitor restart = stated in the UI). The former signals-defaults editor was removed at the same time as the Review waveform chart (2026-07-15).
- **Validation**: the validation / validators aspect selection (`POST /api/v1/config/select`) + the one-click preset list (`GET /api/v1/validation/presets`, pending counts). Execution links to the Validation tab (one function, one place).
- **System** (read-only): deployment facts (ROS_DOMAIN_ID, endpoints, data dir/storage, component health). The version row is omitted because the client has no honest version source. RMW/DDS is not exposed by the API, so only a note is shown.
- **Honest placeholders**: **Dataset profiles** (awaiting the Phase 3 recipe model) and **Users & permissions** (nothing to manage in the single-LAN, no-auth scope) are placeholders that state their reason and nothing more (no dead controls).

## Data flow (SSE × cache)

- Subscribe to the single SSE stream (`GET /api/v1/events`) and fold each event type into the TanStack Query cache. Components subscribe to keys and re-render.
- SSE disconnection is surfaced in the UI (the header connection chip) with automatic reconnection (`Last-Event-ID`).

## Outputs (APIs called)

- Recording: `POST /api/v1/record/prepare` / `start` / `stop`, `GET /api/v1/record/status`
- Batch: `POST /api/v1/batches`, `PATCH /api/v1/batches/{id}`, `GET /api/v1/batches?status=active`, `GET /api/v1/batches/{id}`
- **Capture**: `GET /api/v1/captures` (filters, cursor), `GET /api/v1/captures/{id}`, `PATCH /api/v1/captures/{id}/review`, `POST /api/v1/captures/{id}/delete`, `GET /api/v1/captures/{id}/archive/config`, `POST /api/v1/captures/{id}/archive`
- **Datasets (logical)**: `GET/POST /api/v1/datasets`, `GET/DELETE /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}`, `POST /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/members`, `DELETE /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/members/{membership_id}`
- **Store**: `GET /api/v1/store/health`, `POST /api/v1/store/repair`
- Transfer / retention: `GET /api/v1/transfer/status`, `POST /api/v1/transfer/pull`, `GET /api/v1/retention`
- Topics / system: `GET /api/v1/topics`, `GET /api/v1/topics/status`, `GET /api/v1/events` (SSE), `GET /api/v1/system`
- Config: `GET /api/v1/config`, `GET/PUT /api/v1/config/recording`, `GET /api/v1/config/options`, `POST /api/v1/config/select`, `GET /api/v1/config/robots/{robot}`, `GET/PUT /api/v1/config/alerts`, `GET/PUT /api/v1/plans`
- Files: `GET /api/v1/files/{path}` (video_check mp4 · job artifact images/files)
- Jobs: `GET /api/v1/pipelines`, `POST /api/v1/jobs` (`{ capture_id, pipeline, params }`), `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/status`, `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/result`, `GET/POST /api/v1/validation/templates`, `GET /api/v1/validation/presets`
- **No longer called**: the `/api/v1/runs` family, the `/api/v1/episodes` family, `/api/v1/datasets/{op}/{task}/{index}`, `/api/v1/datasets/export(-all)` (all retired; there are no compatibility aliases)
- Probes (the only two direct connections that do not go through the orchestrator): `/probe` (topics / fields / SSE sample streams), `/webrtc` (offer / ICE)

## Design principles

- **Honesty principle**: never display what cannot be measured (no faked latency / loss; shortfall ≠ loss). Never fabricate a value — a value that cannot be obtained and an evaluation that is not implemented show "—" or an explicit mock label. Never conflate quality with task result. **Never make "could not be read" look like "nothing wrong"** (Store health's empty display, Availability's unknown).
- **Explain a failure in the words of the action that failed.** An error message states not "what happened" but "what became of the thing you just did" (`Not saved.` / `Copied … but it did NOT verify` / a `capture_busy` that names the lease holder). The failure of a destructive operation never becomes a disappearing toast.
- **Non-intrusive**: monitoring display comes from the monitor's raw / no-decode + best_effort path. Payload decoding is isolated in `topic_probe`.
- **Per-screen image-subscription budget**: previews subscribe only while their tab is visible and release on leave; sub cameras are forced to low resolution; aggregate cards (System etc.) use only the orchestrator's API values and never open a new subscription. At most one full-resolution stream at a time.
- No real paths in the frontend / no hardcoded pipelines / schemas and settings are handed over by the backend.
- Endpoints wait for `GET /api/v1/config` to complete before rendering (render gate). Hardcoded fallbacks are dev-only.
- Dangerous operations (double start, topic changes) are suppressed while recording. Destructive operations (Discard / Delete / Reset / End early) always have a confirm modal with Cancel.
- Time-series charts are unified on uPlot.
- Shared configuration: [config](config.md).
